subjects.name: Mathematik
subjects.description: Core subject from Klasse 1 (usually 5 lessons/week in primary school), structured nationally by the KMK Bildungsstandards (end of Kl. 4; ESA/MSA for Sek I) with five Leitideen and six process competences; Länder curricula set the grade placement. Kl. 5–6 is taught in the Orientierungsstufe of the secondary school types (or in primary school in Berlin/Brandenburg).

domains.name: Prozessbezogene Kompetenzen

sources.name: KMK Bildungsstandards für das Fach Mathematik – Primarbereich
sources.notes: Codes constructed by this project in document order (sections 3 and 4 of the document). Process competences: ARG (Mathematisch argumentieren), KOM (kommunizieren), PRO (Probleme mathematisch lösen), MOD (modellieren), DAR (darstellen), OBJ (Mit mathematischen Objekten und Werkzeugen arbeiten) + bullet number. Content: Leitidee prefix ZO/GM/MS/RF/DZ + section (sub-heading under the Leitidee, numbered from 1) + bullet. All bullets of the document are enumerated. Titles are short paraphrases. Note: the 2022 standards require written algorithms only for addition, subtraction and multiplication (ZO.2.7); written division is not part of the standards.

sources.name: KMK Bildungsstandards für das Fach Mathematik – Erster Schulabschluss (ESA) und Mittlerer Schulabschluss (MSA)
sources.level: Ende Jahrgangsstufe 10 (MSA); used here for Kl. 5–6 foundations
sources.notes: Only codes relevant to Kl. 5–6 are listed. Content codes: Leitidee prefix (ZO Zahl und Operation, GM Größen und Messen, FZ Strukturen und funktionaler Zusammenhang, RF Raum und Form, DZ Daten und Zufall) + "M" (the document has no sub-sections; M = bullet list of the Mittlerer-Schulabschluss column) + bullet number in document order (e.g. ZO.M.8 = 8th MSA bullet of Zahl und Operation). Process codes: ARG, KOM, PRO, MOD, DAR, OBJ, MED (Mit Medien mathematisch arbeiten) + Anforderungsbereich (1 Reproduzieren, 2 Zusammenhänge herstellen, 3 Verallgemeinern und Reflektieren) + bullet number. Titles are paraphrases; the standards describe end of Kl. 10, so Kl. 5–6 topics only lay foundations.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Comparing quantities
topics.description: Decide which of two collections has more, fewer or the same number of objects by matching them one-to-one rather than by how spread out they look. A classic Kita/Vorschule precursor skill (Mengenvergleich, Invarianz).
evidence: Pair up objects from two groups one-to-one to decide which group has more
Say that a group still has the same number when its objects are spread out or pushed together
Use the words mehr, weniger and gleich viele correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you put 6 spoons in a long row and 6 cups close together, can {{name}} tell you whether there are more spoons, more cups or the same number of each — and check by matching them up?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Reciting the number word sequence
topics.description: Say the counting words in the correct order, forwards from 1 and backwards from 10, and continue from any number (Weiterzählen) — the verbal basis for all counting.
evidence: Recite the number words from 1 to at least 20 without mistakes
Count on from a given number (e.g. 'start at 7')
Count backwards from 10 to 0 (Countdown)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you say 'Count on from 6', can {{name}} carry on 'seven, eight, nine…' without starting again from one — and can they count backwards from 10 to 0?

osMatches.note: os goes to 100 by age 5-7; this topic is the 1-20 precursor

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Subitising small quantities
topics.description: Recognise small quantities (up to about 4–5) at a glance without counting, and quickly grasp structured quantities such as dice patterns or finger pictures by seeing them as parts (quasi-simultan).
evidence: Name the number of dots on a dice face (1–6) instantly without counting
Show a quantity up to 5 with fingers at once (Fingerbilder)
See 7 dots arranged as 5 and 2 and say 'seven' without counting one by one
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you briefly show {{name}} a dice with five dots, can they say 'five' straight away — without counting each dot?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Counting objects reliably
topics.description: Count a set of objects by assigning exactly one number word to each object and understand that the last word gives the total (Kardinalprinzip); the order of counting does not matter.
evidence: Count up to 20 objects by touching or moving each exactly once
Answer 'How many?' with the last number word said, without recounting
Recognise that counting the same objects in a different order gives the same total
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} counts 12 buttons on the table, do they touch each one once — and when you ask 'how many?', do they answer '12' straight away instead of counting again?

prerequisites.reason: Counting objects requires the stable number word sequence

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Different meanings of numbers
topics.description: Understand that numbers are used in different ways: as a count (Kardinalzahl), as a position (Ordinalzahl: der Dritte), as a measure (5 cm), and as a code (Telefonnummer, Rückennummer). German curricula (e.g. Bayern LehrplanPLUS) make these Zahlaspekte explicit in Klasse 1.
evidence: Sort everyday examples into 'how many', 'which place', 'how long/heavy' and 'just a name/code'
Use ordinal numbers correctly (der Erste, der Dritte in der Reihe)
Explain that a bus number does not tell how many buses there are
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees the number 7 on a football shirt, on a dice and in '7 cm', can they tell you what the 7 means each time?

prerequisites.reason: Cardinal meaning must be secure before contrasting it with other number uses

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Numbers up to 10
topics.description: Read, write and order the numbers 0–10, link numerals, number words and quantities, name neighbours (Vorgänger, Nachfolger) and compare numbers with the symbols <, > and =. Includes learning to write the digits correctly.
evidence: Write the digits 0–9 correctly and match each numeral to a quantity
Name the number before and after any number up to 10
Compare two numbers up to 10 and write the comparison with <, > or =
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} the numbers 7 and 4, can they say which is bigger, write '7 > 4', and tell you which numbers come just before and after 7?

prerequisites.reason: Ordering numbers rests on reliable counting
Quick quantity recognition supports number sense to 10

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Twenty frame and the power of five
topics.description: Use the five- and ten-structure of the Zwanzigerfeld, finger pictures and the Rechenrahmen (bead frame coloured in fives) to see numbers as '5 and some more' and '10 and some more' instead of counting each item — the German didactic principle 'Kraft der Fünf'.
evidence: Show 8 on the twenty frame as a full row of 5 plus 3 without counting singly
Read a quantity laid out in five-structure (e.g. 10 + 5 + 2 = 17) at a glance
Set a number on the Rechenrahmen with one push per colour block
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} a twenty frame with one full row of ten and four more counters, can they say '14' at once without counting each counter?

prerequisites.reason: Numbers to 10 must be known to structure them

osMatches.note: os uses ten-frames; German Zwanzigerfeld/Rechenrahmen emphasise the 5-structure

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Partitioning numbers up to 10
topics.description: Split numbers up to 10 into two parts in all possible ways and record them systematically, typically in a Zahlenhaus (number house) or with Schüttelboxen — the part-whole basis for addition and subtraction.
evidence: Find all decompositions of a number up to 10 (e.g. 7 = 0+7, 1+6, …, 7+0)
Fill in a Zahlenhaus with a missing part
Explain how the decompositions follow a pattern (one part grows, the other shrinks)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} 7 counters and a cup, can they find all the ways the 7 can be split into 'inside the cup' and 'outside the cup' — and write them down in order?

prerequisites.reason: Partitioning works on numbers that are already known

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Number bonds to ten
topics.description: Know by heart the pairs of numbers that make 10 (Zehnerfreunde / verliebte Zahlen) and find the complement to 10 instantly; these facts are the key to the Zehnerübergang.
evidence: Give the complement to 10 for any number 0–10 without counting
Write all pairs that make 10 as additions
Use the twenty frame to show why 6 needs 4 to fill the ten
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you say '7', can {{name}} answer '3' straight away because 7 and 3 make 10?

prerequisites.reason: Bonds to 10 are a special case of number decomposition

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Meaning of addition
topics.description: Understand addition as joining or adding to (hinzufügen, zusammenfügen) and connect actions, pictures and plus equations (Handlung – Bild – Symbol).
evidence: Act out a joining situation with objects and write the matching plus equation
Tell a story that fits a given addition such as 4 + 3
Explain that the result of an addition is the total
topics.assessmentPrompt: If 4 children sit on a bench and 3 more join them, can {{name}} show this with counters and write it as '4 + 3 = 7'?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Meaning of subtraction
topics.description: Understand subtraction as taking away (wegnehmen), as finding the missing part (ergänzen) and as finding a difference (Unterschied) — German textbooks explicitly treat all three Grundvorstellungen.
evidence: Act out a take-away situation and write the minus equation
Solve 'How many more do I need?' as a subtraction or as Ergänzen
Compare two towers and express the difference as a subtraction
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has 9 marbles and loses 4, can they write '9 − 4 = 5' — and can they also see that 'Tom has 9 stickers and Ali 5, how many more has Tom?' is a minus problem?

prerequisites.reason: Subtraction removes or finds a part of a whole
Subtraction is understood in relation to addition

osMatches.note: os focuses on taking away; German topic also covers Ergänzen and Unterschied

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Adding and subtracting within 10
topics.description: Add and subtract within 10 fluently, increasingly from known decompositions rather than counting on fingers one by one.
evidence: Solve additions and subtractions within 10 quickly and correctly
Use known decompositions instead of counting all
Solve a mixed set of plus and minus tasks within 10 in a short time
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} answer '6 + 3' and '8 − 5' quickly — without counting each finger one at a time?

prerequisites.reason: Bonds to 10 make many facts easy

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Commutative pairs
topics.description: Recognise that swapping the numbers in an addition (and later a multiplication) does not change the result, and use the easier order (Tauschaufgabe) to calculate.
evidence: Write the Tauschaufgabe for a given addition
Explain with a picture why 2 + 7 and 7 + 2 give the same result
Choose to calculate 2 + 8 as 8 + 2 by counting on from the larger number
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to work out 2 + 9, do they switch it to 9 + 2 to make it easier — and can they explain why the answer stays the same?

prerequisites.reason: Commutativity is a property of the addition concept

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Inverse problems
topics.description: Understand that subtraction undoes addition and build families of four related tasks (e.g. 3+5, 5+3, 8−5, 8−3) to derive one fact from another.
evidence: Write the Umkehraufgabe for a given addition or subtraction
Complete a family of four related tasks from three numbers
Use an addition fact to solve the matching subtraction
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} knows that 6 + 4 = 10, can they tell you straight away what 10 − 4 and 10 − 6 are — and explain why?

prerequisites.reason: Needs subtraction as reverse of joining

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Missing-number problems
topics.description: Solve problems with an unknown in any position, such as 7 + _ = 12 or _ − 3 = 5, by Ergänzen or by using the inverse task — an early step towards equations.
evidence: Solve 6 + _ = 10 by counting up or by a known bond
Solve problems with the unknown in the first position (_ + 4 = 9)
Explain which inverse task helps to find the missing number
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you write '8 + ☐ = 13', can {{name}} find the missing number and explain how they found it?

prerequisites.reason: Missing-number tasks are solved via inverse tasks
Part-whole thinking identifies the missing part

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Numbers up to 20
topics.description: Read, write, order and represent the numbers to 20 as 'ten and some ones' (Zehner und Einer), locate them in the Zwanzigerfeld and on the Zwanzigerreihe, and compare them.
evidence: Show any number from 11 to 20 as one ten and some ones
Order and compare numbers up to 20
Count forwards and backwards in steps of 1 and 2 within 20
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} to lay out 16 counters, do they make a full ten and six more — and can they say which is bigger, 16 or 19?

prerequisites.reason: The twenty frame shows the ten-structure

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: German number words and digit order
topics.description: German two-digit number words say the ones before the tens (dreiundzwanzig = 'three-and-twenty'), already in the teens (dreizehn). Children learn to write numbers correctly despite this inversion and avoid Zahlendreher (writing 32 for 'zweiunddreißig').
evidence: Write numbers dictated as words (e.g. 'siebenundvierzig') with the digits in the right order
Read two-digit numerals aloud correctly
Explain that in 'achtundfünfzig' the 8 is the ones and the 5 the tens
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you say 'vierundsechzig', does {{name}} write 64 — and not 46?

prerequisites.reason: The inversion starts with the teen numbers

osMatches.note: English number words follow digit order; the inversion problem does not exist there

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Even and odd numbers
topics.description: Recognise even numbers as those that can be split into two equal halves or into pairs, odd numbers as those that leave one over, and spot the pattern in the last digit.
evidence: Sort numbers up to 20 into gerade and ungerade by pairing objects
Predict whether a two-digit number is even from its last digit
Explain why the sum of two even numbers is even
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} 15 socks, can they tell you without counting pairs whether every sock will have a partner — and explain why?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Doubling and halving
topics.description: Know doubles up to 10 + 10 by heart (Verdopplungsaufgaben, e.g. with mirrors or finger pictures) and halve even numbers; doubles are anchor facts for many other tasks.
evidence: Recall all doubles up to 10 + 10 quickly
Halve even numbers up to 20 (later 100)
Use a mirror or the twenty frame to show a double
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you quickly what 7 + 7 is — and what half of 16 is?

osMatches.note: os bundles doubles into general within-20 strategies

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Using neighbouring problems
topics.description: Derive unknown facts from known neighbouring ones, e.g. 6 + 7 from the double 6 + 6 (+1) or 9 + 5 from 10 + 5 (−1) — a core German strategy for 'Ableiten statt Zählen'.
evidence: Solve 7 + 8 via 7 + 7 + 1 and explain the step
Solve 9 + 6 via 10 + 6 − 1
Find the helpful neighbouring task for a given problem
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to work out 8 + 9, do they use something they already know — like 8 + 8 = 16, so one more is 17 — instead of counting?

prerequisites.reason: Doubles are the most common anchor tasks

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Bridging through ten
topics.description: Add and subtract across 10 by splitting the second number to fill or empty the ten first (8 + 5 = 8 + 2 + 3; 13 − 5 = 13 − 3 − 2), shown on the Zwanzigerfeld or Rechenrahmen.
evidence: Solve additions across 10 by stepping to 10 first
Solve subtractions across 10 by stepping back to 10 first
Show the steps on the twenty frame or bead frame
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} works out 7 + 6, can they explain that they first add 3 to make 10 and then add the other 3?

prerequisites.reason: Filling the ten requires bonds to 10
The second number must be split

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Addition facts to 20 by heart
topics.description: Recall all additions and subtractions within 20 automatically (Einspluseins), practised e.g. with 'Blitzrechnen', so that working memory is free for larger calculations.
evidence: Answer any addition or subtraction within 20 within about 3 seconds
Complete a timed sheet of mixed tasks within 20 accurately
Tell which facts they know by heart and which they derive
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you quickly ask {{name}} '8 + 7?' or '15 − 9?', can they answer almost immediately — without counting?

prerequisites.reason: Facts across ten are automatised after strategies are understood
Subtraction facts are linked to addition facts

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Story and picture problems
topics.description: Find the question and the matching plus or minus task in simple story problems and picture problems (Bildsachaufgaben), and write the answer as a sentence.
evidence: Write the matching equation for a picture showing a change situation
Solve a short spoken story problem within 20
Answer with a full sentence that refers back to the story
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you tell {{name}} '5 ducks swim in a pond and 4 more come — how many are there now?', can they write '5 + 4 = 9' and say 'Now there are 9 ducks'?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.reason: Story problems are given orally or as short texts

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Bundling tens and ones
topics.description: Group objects into tens (bundles, Zehnerstangen) and ones, and understand that the position of a digit shows whether it counts tens or ones — the start of the decimal place-value system.
evidence: Bundle a large collection into tens and ones and write the number
Explain the value of each digit in a two-digit number
Exchange one ten for ten ones and back
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} 34 straws and some rubber bands, can they make bundles of ten and tell you that 3 bundles and 4 loose straws make 34?

prerequisites.reason: Ten-and-ones structure is first met in numbers to 20

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Numbers up to 100
topics.description: Read, write, order and compare numbers to 100, count in steps (of 2, 5, 10) from any number, find neighbouring tens, and represent numbers with Zehnerstangen, the Hunderterfeld and the Hunderterrahmen.
evidence: Read and write any number to 100 and say how many tens and ones it has
Order a set of two-digit numbers and find the neighbouring tens
Count forwards and backwards in 1s, 2s, 5s and 10s from any number
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} 'Which number is ten more than 47 — and which tens is 47 between?', can they answer 57 and '40 and 50'?

prerequisites.reason: Two-digit numbers are built from tens and ones
Writing two-digit numbers needs the inversion handled

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Hundred square
topics.description: Use the Hundertertafel (numbers 1–100 in rows of ten) to find numbers, move by tens and ones, and discover number patterns in rows, columns and diagonals.
evidence: Fill in missing numbers in a cut-out piece of the hundred square
Move from a number by +10, −10, +1, −1 on the hundred square
Describe a pattern formed by coloured numbers (e.g. all numbers ending in 5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} a hundred square with one piece missing around 46, can they fill in 36, 45, 47 and 56 — and explain how they knew?

prerequisites.reason: The hundred square displays the numbers to 100

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Base-ten blocks
topics.description: Represent numbers with Einerwürfel, Zehnerstangen, Hunderterplatten and Tausenderwürfel, trade between them, and connect the material to written numerals and the Stellenwerttafel.
evidence: Build a three-digit number with base-ten blocks and write it
Trade ten blocks of one kind for one of the next larger kind
Read a number shown with blocks that are not sorted (e.g. 12 tens and 3 ones)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you lay out 2 hundred-plates, 13 ten-rods and 5 cubes, can {{name}} work out that this is 335?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Number line
topics.description: Locate and read numbers on a scaled Zahlenstrahl (to 100, 1000, 1 000 000), use marked intervals to estimate positions, and find neighbouring numbers.
evidence: Mark given numbers on a number line from 0 to 100 marked in tens
Read off numbers at marked points on a number line to 1000
Estimate the position of a number on a line with only the ends labelled
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you draw a line from 0 to 1000 and point near the middle, can {{name}} estimate that the number there is about 500 — and place 250 sensibly?

prerequisites.reason: Numbers must be known before placing them

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Empty number line for calculating
topics.description: Record mental calculation steps as jumps on an unscaled line (Rechenstrich), e.g. 47 + 28 as +20 and +8, or subtraction by Ergänzen — a German textbook standard for documenting halbschriftliche strategies.
evidence: Show an addition such as 46 + 37 as jumps on a Rechenstrich
Solve a subtraction by Ergänzen with jumps from the smaller to the larger number
Explain someone else's Rechenstrich and write the matching equations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} works out 63 − 28, can they draw a Rechenstrich with jumps and explain each jump?

prerequisites.reason: The empty line abstracts the scaled number line

osMatches.note: os number line topics use scaled lines; the unscaled Rechenstrich is not a separate os topic

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Place-value shorthand
topics.description: Write numbers in Stufenschrift, e.g. 3H 4Z 7E = 347, translate between Stufenschrift, numerals and number words, and handle unusual forms such as 2H 13Z 5E.
evidence: Write a three-digit number in Stufenschrift and back
Convert non-standard forms (e.g. 4H 12Z) into a numeral
Explain why 3Z 5E and 5E 3Z mean the same number
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you write '2H 11Z 4E', can {{name}} work out that this is 314?

prerequisites.reason: Notation for bundled tens and ones

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Analogous problems
topics.description: Transfer basic facts to larger numbers by analogy: from 3 + 4 to 30 + 40 and 23 + 4, from 9 − 5 to 90 − 50 and 59 − 5, without crossing a ten.
evidence: Solve tasks like 50 + 30 and 80 − 60 from the matching basic fact
Solve 34 + 5 and 68 − 3 using the ones fact
Explain the link between 6 + 3 and 46 + 3
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} knows 5 + 3 = 8, can they quickly tell you 50 + 30 and 45 + 3 — and explain why?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Mental strategies within 100
topics.description: Add and subtract two-digit numbers mentally using Schrittweise (stepwise), Stellenweise (place by place), Hilfsaufgabe (compensation, e.g. 47 + 19 = 47 + 20 − 1) and Ergänzen, and choose a strategy that suits the numbers.

Use a Hilfsaufgabe for tasks with 9 or 19
Explain which strategy is quickest for a given task
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} calculates 56 + 29, can they explain a clever way — like adding 30 and taking 1 away?

topics.subject: Mathematik

Draw a dot array for 3 · 6 and read it both ways
Tell a story that fits 4 · 5

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Meaning of division

Act out and write a grouping problem as a division
Explain that 12 : 3 = 4 because 4 · 3 = 12

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Core multiplication facts
topics.description: Know the Kernaufgaben (×1, ×2, ×5, ×10 and square numbers) and derive the other times-table facts from them, e.g. 6 · 7 = 5 · 7 + 1 · 7, using the Malfeld (dot array).

Derive 9 · 6 from 10 · 6 − 6 and explain it on a dot array
Use doubling to get the 4-times facts from the 2-times facts

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Times tables by heart
topics.description: Recall all products of the kleines Einmaleins (1 · 1 to 10 · 10) and the related division facts (Einsdurcheins) automatically; German standards expect this by the end of Klasse 2/3, with tables only up to 10 · 10.

Complete a mixed times-table test accurately

osMatches.note: UK expects tables to 12 × 12 by age 9; German curricula stop at 10 · 10

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Division with remainder

Check a result by 4 · 5 + 3 = 23
Decide in a story whether the remainder means rounding up or leaving out

osMatches.note: os places this at age 9-13; German placement is Kl. 2/3 (age 7-9)

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Word problems with the four operations

Solve a two-step problem and write each step
Write an answer sentence and check whether it makes sense

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Numbers up to 1000

Order a set of three-digit numbers and name neighbouring hundreds
Count forwards and backwards in 10s and 100s from any number

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Place-value chart

Show the effect of adding or removing one counter in a column
Explain why 10 in one column equals 1 in the next column to the left

prerequisites.reason: Chart is used for three-digit numbers and beyond

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Mental calculation up to 1000
topics.description: Add and subtract mentally in the range to 1000 by analogy (e.g. 350 + 400, 670 − 30, 498 + 7) and with simple strategies, without writing intermediate steps.
evidence: Add or subtract multiples of 10 and 100 to three-digit numbers mentally
Bridge a hundred mentally (e.g. 395 + 8)
Find the complement to the next hundred or to 1000
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out in their head what 640 + 70 is, and how much is missing from 380 to 1000?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Informal written addition and subtraction
topics.description: Add and subtract three-digit numbers with written intermediate steps (halbschriftlich): stepwise, place by place, by compensation (Hilfsaufgabe) or by Ergänzen, often recorded on the Rechenstrich.
evidence: Calculate 456 + 278 with written partial steps
Use Ergänzen to solve 702 − 695 quickly
Compare two halbschriftliche strategies for the same task
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} works out 534 − 297, can they write their steps down — for example 534 − 300 + 3 — and explain why it works?

prerequisites.reason: The same strategies are extended to larger numbers

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Multiplying and dividing with multiples of ten
topics.description: Use the times tables for tasks with multiples of 10 and 100 (30 · 4, 7 · 100, 600 : 3, 480 : 8) and understand what happens to the digits when multiplying by 10.
evidence: Calculate tasks such as 6 · 70 and 420 : 6 from times-table facts
Multiply and divide by 10 and 100
Explain with place value why 4 · 30 = 120
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out 8 · 60 and 350 : 7 in their head — and explain which times-table fact helps?

prerequisites.reason: Products are derived from basic facts
Results lie in the range to 1000

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Laws of arithmetic
topics.description: Recognise, explain (e.g. with dot arrays) and use the commutative, associative and distributive laws for clever calculation, such as 4 · 7 · 25 = 7 · 100 or 6 · 14 = 6 · 10 + 6 · 4.
evidence: Explain with a dot array why 6 · 14 = 6 · 10 + 6 · 4
Regroup a sum or product to calculate more easily
Spot which law someone used in a clever calculation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to work out 25 + 38 + 75, do they add 25 and 75 first — and can they explain why that's allowed?

prerequisites.reason: Commutativity is the first law met
Deriving facts already uses the distributive idea

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Informal written multiplication
topics.description: Multiply multi-digit by one-digit (later two-digit) numbers by splitting into place-value parts and recording the partial products, often in a Malkreuz (grid) — e.g. 7 · 38 = 7 · 30 + 7 · 8.
evidence: Calculate 6 · 47 with written partial products
Complete a Malkreuz for 23 · 14
Explain how the partial products relate to the distributive law
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} works out 8 · 36, can they show it as 8 · 30 plus 8 · 6 — for example in a multiplication grid?

prerequisites.reason: Partial products with tens are needed
Splitting relies on the distributive law

osMatches.note: the UK grid method corresponds to the German Malkreuz

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Informal written division
topics.description: Divide multi-digit numbers by one-digit numbers by splitting the dividend into easy multiples (e.g. 156 : 6 = 120 : 6 + 36 : 6) and recording the partial results.
evidence: Divide a three-digit number by a one-digit number with partial steps
Choose a convenient split of the dividend
Check the result by multiplying
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} works out 144 : 6, can they split it into easier parts — for example 120 : 6 and 24 : 6 — and put the results together?

prerequisites.reason: Uses divisions of multiples of ten

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Rounding

evidence: Round three- and four-digit numbers to tens, hundreds and thousands
Explain the rule using the number line
Choose a sensible rounding for prices or distances
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears that 4 678 people came to a match, can they round it to the nearest hundred (4 700) and nearest thousand (5 000)?

prerequisites.reason: Rounding is finding the nearest marked point

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Estimating results
topics.description: Estimate the result of a calculation with rounded numbers before or after calculating exactly, and use the estimate to check written calculations and decide whether an exact result is needed.
evidence: Make an Überschlag for additions, subtractions and multiplications
Detect a wrong result by comparing it with the Überschlag
Decide in a context whether an estimate is enough
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before {{name}} works out 389 + 412 exactly, can they say it will be about 800 — and notice if their written answer of 1801 can't be right?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Column addition
topics.description: Add several multi-digit numbers using the written column algorithm with carrying (Übertrag), writing digits strictly in place-value columns on squared paper (Rechenkästchen), and describe the steps.
evidence: Add two or three numbers with carrying using the column method
Explain what the carried digit means in place-value terms
Find and correct a mistake in a worked column addition
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} adds 368 + 457 in columns, do they line up the digits correctly, carry the ones and tens — and can they explain what the small 1 means?

prerequisites.reason: Digits must be aligned by place value
Informal methods give meaning to the algorithm

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Column subtraction
topics.description: Subtract multi-digit numbers in columns. German schools use different methods: Abziehen mit Entbündeln (decomposition, like the UK), or Ergänzen with Erweitern/Auffüllen ('7 plus wie viel ist 12, 1 gemerkt'), which is spoken as an addition.
evidence: Subtract two multi-digit numbers in columns with regrouping across several places
Explain the borrowing/carrying step of the method used in class
Solve a subtraction with zeros in the minuend (e.g. 1003 − 478)

osMatches.note: UK teaches decomposition only; the German Ergänzungsverfahren has no os counterpart

topics.laenderNotes: Method varies: the long-standing West German standard was the Ergänzungsverfahren (with Erweitern); since the KMK no longer prescribes a method, many Länder/textbooks use Abziehen mit Entbündeln (Bayern LehrplanPLUS names the Abziehverfahren); others leave the choice to the school. Most Länder teach it in Kl. 3, some finish in Kl. 4.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Finding and fixing calculation errors
topics.description: Check calculations with the inverse operation (Probe) and an estimate, find typical errors in worked examples (forgotten carry, column shift, Zahlendreher) and explain how to correct them.
evidence: Check a result with the inverse operation
Find and describe the error in a given wrong calculation
Explain how to avoid a typical error
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} a column subtraction with a mistake in it, can they find the mistake, explain what went wrong and correct it?

The Probe uses the inverse operation

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Choosing calculation methods flexibly
topics.description: Describe, compare and evaluate different ways of solving the same calculation and choose between mental, halbschriftlich and schriftlich methods depending on the numbers (Zahlenblick).
evidence: Solve the same task in two different ways and compare them
Decide for a set of tasks whether to calculate mentally or in writing
Explain why a method is particularly clever for given numbers
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} '1000 − 998', do they see it is quicker to count up 2 than to use the written method — and can they say why?

prerequisites.reason: Requires several strategies to choose from

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Numbers up to one million
topics.description: Read, write, order and represent numbers up to 1 000 000, understand thousands, ten thousands and hundred thousands as continuing the bundling system, and develop a sense of size (e.g. 1000 · 1000).
evidence: Read and write six-digit numbers including zeros (e.g. 304 050)
Order and compare large numbers and place them on a number line
Describe a million in a meaningful way (e.g. 1000 · 1000)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you write '405 080', can {{name}} read it aloud correctly and tell you which number is 1000 more?

prerequisites.reason: Large numbers are organised in the chart

topics.name: Written multiplication

Multiply two multi-digit numbers with correctly shifted partial products
Check the result with an Überschlag

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Written division

Handle zeros in the quotient correctly (e.g. 4 812 : 4)
Check the result by multiplication plus remainder

prerequisites.reason: Gives meaning to the step-by-step algorithm

topics.laenderNotes: Not required by the KMK Bildungsstandards Primarbereich 2022. Bayern GS 3/4 requires it (divisors up to 10, with remainder); NRW and others leave it to Kl. 5 (e.g. NRW G9 Kl. 5); two-digit divisors are usually Kl. 5.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Divisors and multiples
topics.description: Find all divisors of a number (e.g. with dot arrays or Teilerpaare) and its multiples, and use the language 'ist Teiler von', 'ist Vielfaches von'.

List the first multiples of a number and find common multiples
Explain why 7 is a divisor of 42 but not of 45

prerequisites.reason: Divisors and multiples come from the times tables

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Large numbers beyond a million
topics.description: Read, write, round and compare very large numbers in groups of three digits, using the German long-scale names Million (10⁶), Milliarde (10⁹) and Billion (10¹²) — note: the German 'Billion' is the English 'trillion'. Includes number lines with different scales.
evidence: Read and write numbers up to the Billionen correctly
Round large numbers to a sensible place in context (e.g. population figures)
Place large numbers on a number line with a chosen scale

prerequisites.reason: Continues the place-value system beyond a million

topics.name: Roman numerals

Explain the subtraction rule (IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM)
Explain why place value makes calculating easier than Roman numerals

prerequisites.reason: Contrast with the decimal place-value system

topics.laenderNotes: Common Kl. 5 textbook chapter (Bayern Gym 5 mentions it as contrast to the decimal system); some primary textbooks treat it as an optional Exkurs in Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Powers and square numbers
topics.description: Write repeated multiplication as a power (Basis, Exponent), know square numbers up to about 20², and write large numbers with powers of ten (3 · 10⁶).

Recall square numbers up to at least 15²
Write a large number using a power of ten
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you what 3⁴ means and how much it is — and write one Milliarde as a power of ten?

prerequisites.reason: Powers of ten describe large numbers

topics.name: Order of operations and brackets

Name the type of a term (Summe, Produkt …) and draw its Rechenbaum
Write a term with brackets for a word description

prerequisites.reason: Conventions and laws work together when evaluating terms

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Calculating cleverly with arithmetic laws
topics.description: Use the commutative, associative and distributive laws formally to simplify calculations, e.g. 17 · 99 = 17 · 100 − 17 or 4 · 37 · 25, and justify each step.
evidence: Simplify calculations by regrouping and reordering
Use the distributive law in both directions (ausmultiplizieren, ausklammern)
Name the law used in each step
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to calculate 13 · 98, can they use 13 · 100 − 13 · 2 — and name the rule that makes it work?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Divisibility rules
topics.description: Decide divisibility without dividing using Endstellenregeln (2, 4, 5, 10, 25) and Quersummenregeln (3, 9), and justify why the rules work.

Compute the Quersumme and use it for the 3- and 9-rules
Explain why the 2- and 5-rules only need the last digit

topics.name: Prime numbers

Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to list primes up to 100
Explain why 1 is not a prime number

Write the factorisation with powers
Read off all divisors of a number from its factorisation

topics.name: Greatest common divisor and least common multiple

Find them using prime factorisations
Solve a word problem with repeating cycles using the kgV

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Fractions as parts of a whole

topics.name: Fractions of quantities

Convert the result into a smaller unit when needed (3/4 h = 45 min)
Find the whole when a fraction of it is given

topics.name: Fractions on the number line and mixed numbers

Convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers
Explain that 3/3 = 1 and 6/3 = 2

Simplify a fraction completely using the ggT
Decide whether two fractions are equivalent

Order several fractions by size
Use 1/2 as a benchmark for quick comparisons
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you which is bigger, 5/8 or 2/3 — and explain how they decided?

Add mixed numbers and simplify the result

topics.name: Multiplying fractions

Show 'a part of a part' in an area diagram
Simplify crosswise before multiplying

Group numerical data into classes (e.g. heights in 10-cm steps)
Choose and justify a suitable chart type
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} collects the shoe sizes of the class, can they turn the list into a frequency table and choose a good chart for it?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: The mean
topics.description: Calculate the arithmetic mean of a data set and interpret it as 'evening out' (Ausgleichen), and compare it with minimum, maximum, range (Spannweite) and — in some Länder — the median.
evidence: Calculate the mean of a data set
Explain the mean as levelling out towers of cubes
Compare two data sets using mean and range
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} scored 7, 9, 4 and 8 points in four games, can they work out their average — and explain what it tells you?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW G9 Kl. 6 also includes median, range, quartiles and boxplots; Bayern Gym 6 only the arithmetic mean.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Relative frequency
topics.description: Distinguish absolute from relative frequency, calculate relative frequencies as fractions, decimals and percentages, and use them to compare groups of different sizes and to estimate chances.
evidence: Calculate the relative frequency of an outcome as fraction, decimal and percentage
Compare two groups of different sizes using relative frequencies
Use relative frequencies from many trials to estimate a chance
topics.assessmentPrompt: If 12 of 30 children in class 6a and 15 of 25 in 6b walk to school, can {{name}} work out in which class walking is relatively more common?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Pie charts
topics.description: Read and draw pie charts by converting relative frequencies into sector angles (e.g. 25 % = 90°) and judge when a pie chart is suitable.
evidence: Read shares from a pie chart
Draw a pie chart from relative frequencies with compass and Geodreieck
Explain when a pie chart is better than a bar chart
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a third of the class likes football, a quarter swimming and the rest other sports, can {{name}} draw a pie chart for it?

prerequisites.reason: The circle is drawn with a compass

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Evaluating data displays critically
topics.description: Recognise misleading displays (truncated axes, distorted pictures, unequal intervals), compare different displays of the same data, and judge claims made with statistics in the media.
evidence: Explain how a truncated axis exaggerates a difference
Compare two displays of the same data and say which is fairer
Check a media claim against the data shown
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} an advert bar chart where the axis starts at 90, can they explain why the difference looks bigger than it is?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Informatik & Medienbildung
externalPrerequisites.reason: Media literacy is shared with informatics/Medienbildung

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Checking mathematical statements
topics.description: Question mathematical claims ('Stimmt das immer?'), test them with examples, and refute them with a counterexample.
evidence: Test a claim such as 'the sum of two odd numbers is odd' with several examples
Find a counterexample to a false general statement
Say whether examples prove a statement or only support it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a classmate says 'when you add two numbers, the answer is always bigger than both', can {{name}} check it and find a case where it isn't true?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Conjecturing and justifying
topics.description: Formulate conjectures about patterns (e.g. in schöne Päckchen or number walls) and justify them with content-based, visual arguments (inhaltlich-anschauliche Begründungen, e.g. with counters), later with general arguments and variables.
evidence: State a conjecture about a pattern in words
Justify it with a drawing or material (e.g. moving counters)
Follow and evaluate another child's justification
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} notices that in 7+5, 8+4, 9+3 all results are the same, can they explain why with counters or a drawing — not just 'because I checked'?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Explaining and discussing solution paths
topics.description: Describe and explain one's own solution path clearly to others (orally, in writing, with media), follow and question others' paths, and develop solutions together — e.g. in a Rechenkonferenz or Mathekonferenz.
evidence: Explain the steps of one's own solution so that a classmate can follow
Retell and assess a classmate's solution path
Improve a solution together with others
topics.assessmentPrompt: After solving a problem, can {{name}} explain to a friend how they did it step by step — and understand a different way their friend used?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Mathematical vocabulary and symbols
topics.description: Use German mathematical terms and symbols correctly — e.g. Summe/Summand, Differenz/Minuend/Subtrahend, Produkt/Faktor, Quotient/Dividend/Divisor, Ecke/Kante/Fläche, parallel/senkrecht — and translate between symbols and everyday language.
evidence: Name the parts of a calculation with the correct terms
Read an equation aloud in words and write a word statement as an equation
Use geometric terms correctly when describing a figure
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you write '56 : 8 = 7', can {{name}} tell you which number is the Dividend, the Divisor and the Quotient?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.reason: Mathematical terms are part of academic German

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Problem-solving strategies
topics.description: Tackle unfamiliar problems by using heuristics — systematisches Probieren, Rückwärtsarbeiten, Analogien nutzen, Skizze, Tabelle — and review and adapt the approach when it does not work.
evidence: Solve a non-routine problem by systematic trial and improvement
Work backwards from a given result
Change strategy when the first approach fails and explain why
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} a puzzle they haven't seen before, do they try something systematic — like a table or working backwards — and change approach if they get stuck?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Extracting relevant information
topics.description: Extract the information relevant to a question from texts, pictures, tables and real situations, distinguish it from superfluous information, and notice when information is missing.
evidence: Mark the relevant numbers in a word problem
Identify superfluous information
Say which information is missing to answer a question
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a word problem contains a number that isn't needed, does {{name}} notice it — and can they tell you what extra information they would need for an unanswerable question?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Mathematical modelling
topics.description: Translate a real situation into mathematics (simplify, choose operations, make assumptions), work mathematically, interpret the result in the situation and check its plausibility — the modelling cycle.
evidence: Make reasonable assumptions to simplify a real situation
Translate a situation into a calculation and solve it
Interpret the result and check whether it makes sense
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} how much water the family uses for showers in a week, can they decide what they need to know, estimate it, calculate and judge whether the answer is realistic?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Inventing word problems
topics.description: Invent stories and word problems that fit a given calculation, equation or picture, and check whether a given story fits a calculation.
evidence: Tell a story that fits 12 − 5
Write a word problem for a given multiplication
Decide which of several stories fits a given equation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you write '4 · 3 = 12', can {{name}} make up a little story that fits it?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.reason: Written word problems are short texts

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Switching between representations
topics.description: Choose and use suitable representations (material, picture, symbol, table, sketch), translate one into another — Handlung, Bild, Symbol — and compare which representation helps most.
evidence: Show a calculation with material, as a picture and as an equation
Translate a drawing into a calculation and vice versa
Explain which representation makes a problem easiest
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} '3 · 4', can they show it with counters, draw it, and tell a story — and say which way makes it clearest?

prerequisites.reason: First operations shown in several forms

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Fermi problems
topics.description: Solve open estimation problems without given numbers (e.g. 'How many children fit in the schoolyard?') by making assumptions, using benchmarks, estimating and calculating, and compare different approaches.
evidence: Break a Fermi question into measurable or estimable parts
Make and justify assumptions
Compare the estimate with others and discuss differences
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} 'How many sheets of paper does our class use in a year?', can they come up with a sensible estimate and explain their steps?

prerequisites.reason: Fermi problems are open modelling tasks

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Using digital maths tools
topics.description: Use digital tools purposefully — e.g. apps with virtual materials, a calculator for checking, simple dynamic geometry software and spreadsheets for data — and judge when a tool helps.
evidence: Represent data with a spreadsheet or app
Draw and vary a figure with geometry software
Decide sensibly when a calculator is appropriate and check its result
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} enters class data into a spreadsheet, can they make a chart from it — and explain when using a calculator would or wouldn't make sense?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Understanding algorithms
topics.description: Recognise written calculation methods, constructions and step-by-step rules as algorithms, describe them precisely, follow and correct them, and invent simple ones ('unplugged').
evidence: Describe the written addition as an exact sequence of steps
Follow a step-by-step instruction and find an error in it
Write instructions for a construction that someone else can follow
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write down exact instructions for column addition — so precisely that a classmate can follow them without asking?

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is building the foundations of number: comparing groups, recognising small amounts at a glance and counting objects reliably.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind legt Grundlagen für Zahlen: Mengen vergleichen, kleine Anzahlen auf einen Blick erkennen und sicher abzählen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is learning numbers to 20 and then 100, splitting numbers into parts, adding and subtracting with clever strategies instead of counting, and learning the times tables.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Zahlen bis 20 und bis 100, zerlegt Zahlen, rechnet plus und minus mit geschickten Strategien statt zu zählen und lernt das Einmaleins.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is working with numbers up to a million, calculating mentally and with written steps, learning the written (column) methods and checking answers by estimating.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind arbeitet im Zahlenraum bis zur Million, rechnet im Kopf und halbschriftlich, lernt die schriftlichen Rechenverfahren und überprüft Ergebnisse mit dem Überschlag.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about large numbers, divisibility and prime numbers, and — for the first time systematically — fractions, decimals, percentages and negative numbers.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschäftigt sich mit großen Zahlen, Teilbarkeit und Primzahlen sowie – erstmals systematisch – mit Brüchen, Dezimalzahlen, Prozenten und negativen Zahlen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child compares things by length, weight and size by putting them side by side.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind vergleicht Dinge nach Länge, Gewicht und Größe, indem es sie direkt nebeneinanderlegt.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to measure with a ruler, handle euros and cents, read the clock and use the calendar.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt mit dem Lineal zu messen, mit Euro und Cent umzugehen, die Uhr zu lesen und den Kalender zu nutzen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is learning all everyday units (mm to km, g to t, ml and l, seconds to years), converting them, using benchmarks to estimate, and solving word problems with measures.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Alltagseinheiten (mm bis km, g bis t, ml und l, Sekunden bis Jahre), rechnet sie um, schätzt mit Stützpunktvorstellungen und löst Sachaufgaben mit Größen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is calculating perimeter, area and volume with formulas and learning area and volume units such as m², ha and cm³.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind berechnet Umfang, Flächeninhalt und Volumen mit Formeln und lernt Flächen- und Volumeneinheiten wie m², ha und cm³.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is spotting and continuing simple repeating patterns.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind erkennt einfache Muster und setzt sie fort.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child explores number patterns with typical formats such as number walls, arithmetic triangles and structured problem sets, and learns what the equals sign really means.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind erforscht Zahlenmuster mit typischen Formaten wie Zahlenmauern, Rechendreiecken und schönen Päckchen und lernt, was das Gleichheitszeichen bedeutet.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child compares expressions, explores codes and growing patterns, and solves problems where one quantity depends on another, like amount and price.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind vergleicht Terme, erkundet Verschlüsselungen und wachsende Muster und löst Aufgaben, in denen eine Größe von einer anderen abhängt, etwa Menge und Preis.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is starting to use letters for numbers, writing simple terms and equations, and solving proportion problems with the rule of three.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind verwendet erstmals Variablen, stellt einfache Terme und Gleichungen auf und löst Zuordnungsaufgaben mit dem Dreisatz.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is learning words for where things are: above, below, next to, between, left and right.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Wörter für die Lage von Dingen: oben, unten, neben, zwischen, links und rechts.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is naming flat shapes and solids, laying and folding shapes, describing routes and discovering symmetry.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind benennt Flächen und Körper, legt und faltet Formen, beschreibt Wege und entdeckt die Achsensymmetrie.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child builds cube buildings from plans, works with cube nets, draws with the Geodreieck and compass, reflects and enlarges figures, and measures area and volume by counting units.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind baut Würfelgebäude nach Bauplänen, arbeitet mit Würfelnetzen, zeichnet mit Geodreieck und Zirkel, spiegelt und vergrößert Figuren und bestimmt Flächen- und Rauminhalte durch Auslegen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is learning precise geometry: angles, the coordinate system, special triangles and quadrilaterals, and reflections, rotations and translations.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt präzise Geometrie: Winkel, Koordinatensystem, besondere Dreiecke und Vierecke sowie Spiegelungen, Drehungen und Verschiebungen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child sorts objects by colour, shape or size and explains the rule.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind sortiert Gegenstände nach Farbe, Form oder Größe und erklärt die Regel.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child collects data with tally charts, reads simple tables and charts, and describes events as certain, possible or impossible.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind sammelt Daten mit Strichlisten, liest einfache Tabellen und Diagramme und beschreibt Ereignisse als sicher, möglich oder unmöglich.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child plans small surveys, draws bar charts, counts possibilities systematically and compares chances in games.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind plant kleine Befragungen, zeichnet Säulendiagramme, zählt Möglichkeiten systematisch und vergleicht Gewinnchancen.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child organises data in frequency tables, calculates averages and relative frequencies, draws pie charts and learns to spot misleading diagrams.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind ordnet Daten in Häufigkeitstabellen, berechnet Mittelwerte und relative Häufigkeiten, zeichnet Kreisdiagramme und erkennt irreführende Diagramme.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to explain how they calculated, to check whether statements are true, to switch between objects, pictures and numbers, and to make up their own story problems.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt zu erklären, wie es gerechnet hat, Aussagen zu prüfen, zwischen Material, Bild und Zahl zu wechseln und eigene Rechengeschichten zu erfinden.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child uses problem-solving strategies, picks out the important information in real situations, models everyday problems mathematically (including Fermi estimates) and uses digital tools.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind nutzt Problemlösestrategien, entnimmt wichtige Informationen aus Sachsituationen, modelliert Alltagsprobleme (auch Fermi-Aufgaben) und nutzt digitale Werkzeuge.

clusters.subject: Mathematik
clusters.summary: Your child justifies conjectures with general arguments, works through the modelling cycle more independently and describes procedures precisely as algorithms.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind begründet Vermutungen allgemein, durchläuft den Modellierungskreislauf selbstständiger und beschreibt Verfahren präzise als Algorithmen.
